newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada moves closer to alliance with Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: Canada moves closer to alliance with Mercosur.

text.p: Canada and South American trade bloc Mercosur are one step closer to forming an alliance, Argentine trade minister Alieto Guadagni said on Monday.

Canada and Mercosur countries -- Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Brazil -- will begin an exchange of official documents next month, laying out their positions to make Canada an associate member of the trade bloc, Guadagni said.
"Canada will be welcome," he told reporters after meeting with Canada's new trade minister Sergio Marchi. "We want to profit from this relationship."

Canada would not be a full member of Mercosur but would have an associate membership much like Chile or Bolivia, Guadagni said, adding that Mercosur countries would be able to benefit from direct investment from Canada, access to a large and rich market and advanced technology.

Canada would benefit from lower tariffs for its exports to the Mercosur countries while its biggest competitor -- the United States -- is held back because of its lack of fast-track negotiating authority. Canada has already negotiated its own free trade agremeent with Chile.

There are no negotiations between Mercosur and the United States for now, Guadagni said. The United States has concentrated on negotiations for a free trade zone that would include all of North and South America.
The Free Trade Agreement of the Americas is supposed to be in force by 2005, but the Mercosur countries have resisted U.S. pressure to move quickly on the agreement.

Guadagni reiterated his allegiance to the Mercosur policy. "Mercosur must be the building block of this agreement," he said. "We do not think Mercosur will disappear. It will maintain its own personality."
Guadagni also said that Argentina's plan to introduce a 0.5 percent tariff on imports from non-Mercosur nations was not written in stone.
"It's not decided yet," he said. "The final decision has not been taken."
